description: The true path of the miniature: two statements that cannot both hold, one of them against the narrator's own observation; that statement distrusted, and the question it was told to cover answered by who could reach the box.

moves.see: nobody came in from the yard
moves.why: The back door is the only way in from the yard, and it did not open.
So nobody came in at the back door at half past two: what the Captain said he saw did not happen.
The Captain's is the statement my own afternoon contradicts.
Nothing I saw myself is against what Mr. Fenn said.

moves.see: by the front door after one
moves.why: The front door was locked from one, and I had the key.

moves.see: nobody came in from the yard
moves.why: And the back door never opened.

moves.see: Mr. Fenn was outside from one
moves.why: Mr. Fenn went out while the box was still full, and no door let him back.

moves.see: the Captain was inside the whole time
moves.why: The Captain never left the house.
Nobody came in, Mr. Fenn was out, and I did not rob myself: only the Captain could reach the box.
He was outside both doors from one o'clock.
